title: SLO-driven evidence collector and compact postmortem generator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an automated incident 'evidence collector' that assembles a compact, SLO-aware evidence bundle when an alert breaches an SLO window. The bundle should include representative traces, top error logs, metric rollups, and suggested runbook steps; it should be attached to PagerDuty incidents and posted into the on-call Slack channel as a condensed summary. The goal is to reduce time-to-triage by surfacing probable root causes and the minimal set of artifacts an on-call engineer needs to act, and to seed a first-draft postmortem document with a filled timeline and suggested RCA hypotheses.
acceptance_criteria: When an alert breaches configured SLO threshold, system creates an evidence bundle with: 1 representative high-latency trace, 3 top error logs, a 5-minute metric delta for related metrics, and top 5 affected routes/keys.
Evidence bundle is uploaded to the incident channel and attached to the PagerDuty incident with a short summary and deep links to traces/logs.
A draft postmortem is created and pre-populated with: incident timeline (auto-sourced), impacted services list, severity justification, and two suggested RCA hypotheses inferred from traces/metrics.
RBAC respects Private deployments: bundles in VPC/on-prem do not leak raw logs to hosted storage; links reference customer-managed artifacts as configured.
Operation toggle: teams can opt out of draft postmortem creation or limit which data types are included by policy.
End-to-end tests demonstrate <30s additional latency on alert path and no change to primary SLO evaluation.
Security review sign-off on data retention and KMS usage for attachments.
design_decisions: Bundle size: choose compact JSON summary (<= 200KB) + links to full artifacts rather than including full logs to reduce PD/Slack payloads and preserve privacy.
Representative trace selection: prefer highest-error-density trace within the breach window, then highest-p90 latency if no errors.

RCA suggestion heuristic: combine span-level error signals, anomalous metric deltas, and recent deploys to rank hypotheses; do not claim certainty — present as 'top hypotheses' with supporting evidence.
Security: redact sensitive fields from log snippets by default; allow team policy to toggle redaction strictness for Private deployments.
Delivery: implement pipeline as independent microservice that subscribes to observability event bus to decouple from alerting flow and allow retries.
tradeoffs: Embedding full logs in the PD/Slack attachments simplifies triage but risks leaking sensitive data and increases payload sizes. We choose links + compact snippets to balance usability and safety.
Generating draft postmortems automatically speeds incident writeup but may create noise for false positives; we add an opt-out and require explicit Acknowledgement to publish final postmortem.
Doing heavy analysis synchronously in alert path would increase alert latency; moving analysis to an async evidence-collector adds eventual consistency but preserves SLOs.
open_questions: What is the canonical format for the evidence bundle so downstream tools (runbooks, postmortem template) can parse consistently?
Should we allow customers to provide custom extractors for application-specific fields?
How long should we persist draft postmortems and evidence bundles by default for hosted customers (30/90/365 days)?
What rate limits do PagerDuty and Slack impose on attachments and how should we back off to avoid throttling during flapping incidents?
implementation_plan: Week 1: design doc and API contract for evidence bundle (Confluence link in links).
Week 2: implement bundle assembler service and unit tests; mock observability events locally.
Week 3: integrate with PD/Slack caller libraries; add RBAC and redaction pipeline for Private deployments.
Week 4: end-to-end integration test and staged rollout to internal teams; gather feedback and iterate.
Week 5: public beta with two customers and final security/compliance sign-off.
